prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1427; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by phone from the insured's household member, who was driving the insured vehicle when it was struck while turning left at an intersection. The driver reports neck and back pain and says the other vehicle came through on the opposing lane as the turn was being made.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is a resident of the policyholder's household and is listed as a covered operator under the policy. Coverage for this loss appears to be in force, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle in the intersection and records that the claimant was seated behind the wheel at the scene. Officer notes describe the impact location consistent with the driver's account.

Entry 4: Photographs of the insured vehicle show front-quarter damage that lines up with the described impact. No prior body damage or repair records were found in the vehicle history.

Entry 5: Spoke with two independent witnesses from the intersection. Both recall the sequence of the collision the same way the claimant described it, and neither had any connection to the parties.

Entry 6: Contacted the other driver, who confirmed the account of how the collision happened and acknowledged responsibility for the turn-across path. Their statement matches the scene diagram and the witness accounts.

Entry 7: Claimant is now represented by counsel, who has requested that all further contact be routed through their office. Injury description has been sent for review, with neck and back strain noted as the initial diagnosis.

Entry 8: Medical records show a treatment course running somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of soft tissue injury. Imaging was ordered and the physician's notes indicate no earlier complaints involving the same areas of the spine.

Entry 9: Reviewed the claimant's statements across the recorded call, the written statement, and the interview with counsel present. The account of the collision and the sequence of events has stayed the same in each of them.

Entry 10: Reviewed the injury and the impact forces together. The reported neck and back strain fits the type and force of the crash, and the file is ready to move forward for valuation pending the remaining treatment records.
